records.name: Pomeranian Voivodeship
records.summary: No voivodeship-level trans-specific resolution, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division in the current research pass. The anti-LGBT municipal-resolution wave (80+ municipalities and four voivodeship-level declarations as of March 2020) concentrated in the eastern and south-eastern parts of the country, so the absence of local findings here indicates thinner documentation rather than established safety. The national frame governs this division: no hate-crime protection on sexual-orientation or gender-identity grounds (the March 2025 amendment bill referred to the Constitutional Tribunal, hearings held July and September 2025), court-based and medically gatekept legal gender recognition, and national sources documenting a trans foreign woman held in a male-only guarded detention centre and an ECtHR ruling that denying a prisoner hormone therapy violates private life.

records.name: Silesian Voivodeship
records.summary: This division appears in the national court history of the anti-LGBT municipal-resolution wave: the provincial administrative court sitting in Gliwice ruled on the Istebna gmina resolution, and the Supreme Administrative Court's ruling of 28 June 2022 dismissed the appeals of four municipalities whose annulments had been ordered below, holding that the resolutions "violate the dignity" of LGBT people (an earlier May 2022 ruling held they "pose a risk of violence against LGBT people"). Otherwise no voivodeship-level trans-specific incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division in the current research pass — the municipal-resolution wave concentrated elsewhere. The national frame governs: no hate-crime protection on sexual-orientation or gender-identity grounds (the March 2025 amendment bill referred to the Constitutional Tribunal), court-based and medically gatekept legal gender recognition, and national sources documenting a trans foreign woman held in a male-only guarded detention centre and an ECtHR ruling that denying a prisoner hormone therapy violates private life.

records.name: Cross River
records.summary: No state-specific trans-related source was found for this division in the current research pass: no local incident series and no documented enforcement divergence from the national frame. The national law applies here in full — the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (up to 14 years, extends to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression of identity) plus the inherited criminal provisions; national monitoring recorded 89 extortions, 118 harassment incidents and more than 20 unlawful detentions of LGBTQ+ people by law-enforcement officials in 2024 alone, with detentions for "looking gay" and release on payment of a bribe reported. This division sits outside the twelve northern states that carry a separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct. Dating-app "kito" extortion gangs are a nationwide app-user risk, and foreign government travel advice warns LGBT travellers of arrest, violence and blackmail.

records.name: Ogun
records.summary:
No regional protective statute, recorded incident series or documented enforcement divergence from the national framework has been documented for this state. The national framework applies in full: a 2014 statute punishes same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment and — as reported in August 2026 summarising a foreign government's travel advisory — also reaches assisting, attending or promoting same-sex ceremonies and LGBT+ organisations; religious criminal law in some northern states can carry the death penalty for same-sex conduct. The same advisory warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation.

The recorded violence pattern is national and recent: a 33-year-old transgender media personality and sex worker was beaten to death in the federal capital in August 2024, having reported a stabbing a year earlier and said she feared for her life; authorities ordered a discreet investigation. Mass arrests and detention of LGBT+ people remain common, concentrated in some northern states. The framework also bans public expression of identity and LGBT+ organising, and the advisory additionally flags short-notice curfews, network shutdowns and communal violence. The absence of state-specific records here reflects thin documentation rather than demonstrated safety.
